text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a new regression after the kernel-selector v3 roll that affects KV cache page-table mapping on long-context runs (>32k tokens) on mixed A100/H100 clusters. Repro attached below.

alex: Symptoms: steady VRAM growth per request (~20–40MB) and PT entry counts climbing even after requests finish. Only happens when_page_migration is enabled + continuous batching.

alex: Repro (quick):
```
# run on a 2xH100 + 2xA100 machine (nvlink off for A100s in this env)
./repro_longctx.sh --model redwood/v1-epoch --tokens 35000 --batch 8 --enable-page-migration
```
Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T12:02:10Z] kvcache: alloc_page_table idx=10234 owner=worker-7 map_flags=0x3
[2026-03-18T12:02:10Z] kvcache: pt_refcount[10234]=1
[2026-03-18T12:02:12Z] kvcache: evict_page idx=10234 deferred=true
[2026-03-18T12:02:12Z] kvcache: pt_refcount[10234]=2  <-- unexpected bump
[2026-03-18T12:02:14Z] kvcache: map_check failed at idx=10234 expected_owner=worker-7 found_owner=nil
```

alex: Looks like the kernel-selection path for PagedAttention changed the _allocation vs mapping_ order on H100 (we now touch the KV tile with kernel A before recording the PT owner) which leaves a transient window where another thread re-maps the same slot. On MI250x we see a slightly different timing where the pt_refcount never drops because the unmap path skips decrement when the page is in migration state.

priya: :eyes: can you paste the small repro (repro_longctx.sh) or point to the test job? I want to run on our CI farm (mi250x node).

alex: Pushed to /infra/repros/kvcache/6294 — script is tiny, it spawns concurrent requests with pinned context lengths and toggles page_migration. The critical change is kernel-selector v3 picks the "tiling/warp-first" kernel on H100 which invokes kvcache.touch_before_owner_set().

sam: Have we seen similar refcount leaks before? I remember a shadowmap case but not exactly this flow. Could be the `touch_before_owner_set` ordering bug.

carla: If the refcount increases after evict and never goes back, we can force a guard in the unmap path to decrement on migration rollback. Quick mitigation: in pagetable.c add a SAFE_DEC on unmap when state==MIGRATING. That will stop growth but might hide real races.

alex: Agreed — I'd prefer to patch touch order so owner is set atomically before any kernel touches the tile. But need to confirm NV vs AMD differences: on MI250x we saw extra queue depth from ROCm scheduler that repeatedly issues map/unmap pairs, so the unmap path needs to be robust.

priya: Running CI now on mi250x + h100 pair. Will report results in ~10m.

infra-bot: Job 48291 started: kvcache-longctx-repro on mi250x/h100 (2x each). Link: https://ci.internal/jobs/48291

sam: Also add a small assert into map() to detect double-map windows:
```
if (owner == NONE) {
  owner = current_worker;
} else {
  BUG_ON(owner != current_worker, "double-map race owner=%d cur=%d", owner, current_worker);
}
```
That will crash CI fast if race exists.

carla: If CI repros, I'll prepare a minimal patch: (A) set owner under lock before dispatching kernels, (B) SAFE_DEC in unmap as stopgap, (C) add telemetry metric pt_leak_count++.

alex: Thanks. If we can get a failing trace, please also capture `cuda_meminfo` / `rocclr_meminfo` at 1s intervals — we need exact VRAM deltas. I suspect this only surfaces with continuous batching + prefix caching.

priya: CI finished: reproduced on MI250x, not repro on H100-only machines (without A100s). Logs: pt_refcount counters climb to ~4500 across lifetime. Linking CI logs: https://ci.internal/logs/48291/trace.txt

sam: Interesting that H100-only doesn't repro — suggests ordering diff on the kernel path isn't identical across archs. Might be queuing differences. Good catch.

alex: I'll open a fix PR against runtime/kernel-selector to set owner before launching any kernel that can touch pages. Assigning @carla for the unmap guard follow-up.

carla: I'll draft the PR, include perf test and pt_leak telemetry. Will also add a health-check that runs the repro in nightly so we don't regress again.

alex: Awesome. Follow-ups: (1) patch owner ordering (PR 9321), (2) add SAFE_DEC guard (PR 9322), (3) nightly repro job.

priya: Thanks everyone — temporary workaround for customers: disable page_migration or reduce batching to avoid the timing window.

sam: Note for release notes: "Fixed KV cache page-table refcount leak under long context runs on MI250x with page migration enabled."

alex: closing loop here once PRs land. :thumbsup:
